subject: Conversation flow stuttering — mitigation steps and post-incident summary
messages:
From: Chris Ramos <chris.ramos@novusai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent stutter on streaming/chat endpoint — urgent

Hi Markus,

We started seeing intermittent "stuttering" in our production live-chat sessions this afternoon (first observed ~22:40 UTC). Roughly 5-8% of sessions exhibit 3–8s stalls where no tokens arrive for a period and then the remainder of the response streams through. Users report the experience as a brief hang followed by a burst of text.

Affected: our streaming/chat route using model alias rwd-v1.2 (streaming=true), primarily hitting the us-west region. I've attached a session trace (session_trace_20261003.txt) that includes two session IDs and timestamps showing the gaps.

Impact: noticeable UX regression for our support chat during a peak period (we saw an uptick in abandoned chats). This started after your last update window a few hours ago — not sure if related.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has any known incidents, and advise short-term mitigations we can apply on our side while you investigate? If you have a recommended client fallback or timeout pattern to reduce user impact, please share it.

Thanks — this is live for a key product demo tomorrow, so any immediate guidance helps.

— Chris
Chris Ramos
Head of Platform Ops, NovusAI
ops@novusai.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intermittent stutter on streaming/chat endpoint — urgent

Chris — thanks for the trace and the heads up. We're seeing matching spikes in streaming tail latency for the us-west fleet and have opened an incident ticket (JIRA-INF-8345) to track this. Immediate notes and mitigations below.

Short-term client-side mitigations (apply now):
- Set stream_chunk_timeout=500ms in our SDK so the client treats small gaps as deliverable rather than hanging UI.
- Enable client fallback mode: if no bytes for >2.5s, call generate() non-streaming for a single retry.
- If you can, reduce default max_tokens per request by ~20% for high-concurrency chat sessions to lower token emission bursts.

What we're doing on our side (immediate):
- Triage running now; engineering is collecting kernel and KV cache metrics for the affected shards.
- We'll push a targeted config rollback to a canary subset (us-west-2) to revert a batching parameter change that looks suspicious.
- I'll follow up with a short postmortem and recommended permanent fixes by tomorrow EOD.

Can you share 2–3 representative session IDs from the trace (I highlighted two but more helps)? I just need the session start timestamps and IDs.

Date: Sat, 04 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Triage: Conversation flow stuttering — INF-8345

Team —

Summary: NovusAI reported intermittent streaming stalls in us-west (see ticket JIRA-INF-8345). I reviewed the session traces and early telemetry. Observable symptoms: token emission gaps of 3–8s with subsequent burst. Incidence peaked between 21:00–23:00 UTC on 2026-10-03.

What we observed so far:
- KV cache churn and elevated miss rates on a small subset of shards after the 14:00 UTC config canary.
- The recent dynamic-batching alpha increase (0.6) reduced average latency for medium sequences but increased batch headroom variance; this appears to have exposed a cache eviction pattern for long-lived sessions.
- No hardware failures; network telemetry is clean.

Immediate actions taken (done at 07:45 PT):
- Reverted dynamic-batching alpha from 0.6 -> 0.45 for the canary pool in us-west-2.
- Increased per-shard KV cache allocation by +25% for affected hosts.
- Enabled aggressive prefix-KV warmup during active sessions.

Short-term recommendations to stabilize (please prioritize):
- Roll forward the alpha rollback to all us-west production shards (Sofia/Ben to confirm safe window).
- Temporarily pin NovusAI traffic to model variant rwd-v1.2-q4 (quantized variant) which shows lower memory churn under identical load.
- Add a server-side guard: if stream stall > 4s, emit a small keepalive chunk to prevent client UI timeouts while we rebuild caches.

Attachments: engine_trace_20261004.log (excerpted logs showing eviction spikes).

Priority: high — NovusAI has a major demo tomorrow. Please let me know ETA for full us-west rollout of the rollback and whether we can safely increase KV cache limits cluster-wide for the next 48 hours.

— Markus

Date: Sat, 04 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & guidance — streaming stalls (us-west)

Chris — thanks again for the quick escalation and the trace. Here is a concise post-incident summary and concrete next steps for NovusAI.

What happened (root cause):
- During a routine canary of an increased dynamic-batching alpha, we observed elevated KV cache eviction on a subset of us-west shards. That eviction caused intermittent pauses in token emission for long-lived streaming sessions while the cache was rebuilt, which manifested as the 3–8s "stutters" you saw.

What we did (mitigations applied):
- Reverted dynamic-batching alpha 0.6 -> 0.45 across all us-west shards (completed 2026-10-04 07:50 PT).
- Increased per-shard KV cache allocation (+25%) in the short term and enabled prefix warmup for active sessions.
- Added a server-side keepalive emission for streaming sessions when a stall exceeds 4s.
- Opened a tracking ticket: JIRA-INF-8345 (link: JIRA-INF-8345). Postmortem doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1XyPostmortemDoc (postmortem_20261004.pdf attached).

Customer-facing mitigations (what you can do now):
- Set stream_chunk_timeout=500ms in the SDK to reduce perceived UI hangs.
- Configure a fallback: if no streamed bytes for >2.5s, call a single non-streaming generate() retry.
- Optionally reduce max_tokens by ~20% for high-concurrency sessions during your next peak.

What we're changing long-term:
- We'll adjust batching alpha rollout procedures to include KV-cache churn tests in canaries.
- Improve automated detection to emit keepalive chunks before cache rebuilds finish.
- We'll provide a small client SDK update that exposes sensible stream timeouts and a built-in safe fallback pattern.

Next steps and timeline:
- Engineering will complete a full postmortem and RCA doc today and share by EOD.
- We'll keep the short-term cache increase and keepalive enabled for 48 hours while we validate stability, then revert if safe.
- I'll propose a brief compensatory credit for the inconvenience; I'll follow up with the commercial lead early next week.

If you want, we can schedule a 20–30 minute call this afternoon to walk your team through the mitigations and update your engineers on SDK knobs.

Thanks for the fast signal — we pushed the rollback and mitigations quickly once you reported it.

— Markus
